title: Affine-component etale hypercovers of arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $T$ be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is an augmented simplicial scheme [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] $v:V_\bullet\to T$ with $V_n=\coprod_{i\in I_n}V_{n,i}$ and every $V_{n,i}$ affine. Every structure map sends each specified summand into one specified summand, with the compatible component-index maps, and each $V_n\to T$ is etale. The matching morphisms $V_n\to M_n(V_\bullet/T)$ are surjective etale; here $M_0=T$, and $M_n$ is the finite limit of compatible proper faces in schemes over $T$. For any algebraic space $X\to T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $X\times_T V_\bullet\to X$ is an etale hypercover with the same decompositions pulled back. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $T$ is imposed. Given any etale hypercover $H_\bullet\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-hypercover], such a $V_\bullet$ can be chosen with a simplicial refinement $V_\bullet\to H_\bullet$. More precisely, one may choose this refinement split: there are subsets $N_r\subseteq I_r$ of nondegenerate indices and decompositions $I_n=\coprod_{[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]}N_r$, and the summand labelled by $(\sigma,i)$ is a copy of $V_{r,i}$ with its map to $H_n$ equal to $V_{r,i}\to H_r\xrightarrow{H(\sigma)}H_n$. Given affine open covers of all $H_r$, the map $V_{r,i}\to H_r$ for every $i\in N_r$ can be required to factor through a member of the prescribed degree-$r$ cover. This condition is imposed on nondegenerate summands; the degenerate copies have the displayed forced maps.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal C=T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and its category of formal families. The finite-limits theorem gives matching families $M_n(K)$, computed from the finitely many proper faces even for a truncated $K$. The singleton family associated to a simplicial etale $T$-scheme $H$ has matching family $\{M_n(H)\}$: its index diagram consists of singletons and the component limit is the scheme limit. This follows directly from the terminal-object and fibre-product formulas, or the compatible-face description of matching objects. Thus a truncated map $K\to H$ gives $M_n(K)\to\{M_n(H)\}$. No finiteness of the sets indexing the families is used.

Fix a target hypercover $H$. In degree zero choose an affine open cover of $H_0$ refining its prescribed cover. Its members form $K_0$, with their maps to $H_0$ and $T$. The affine-basis theorem supplies the refinement by taking affine neighbourhoods inside each prescribed open. Open immersions are etale; composition of covering families shows $K_0\to T$ is a covering. A degree-zero family is split, since its only degeneracy label is the identity.

Inductively suppose $K$ is split through degree $n-1$, with affine components, matching coverings and a map to $H$ in the retained degrees. Write $M_n(K)=\{P_a\}_a$. Pull back the surjective etale map $H_n\to M_n(H)$ along $P_a\to M_n(H)$, obtaining $R_a=P_a\times_{M_n(H)}H_n\to P_a$. It is a surjective etale scheme morphism by covering base change. Cover each inverse image in $R_a$ of a prescribed affine open of $H_n$ by affine open neighbourhoods. Together these give an affine family $A_n$ mapping to the relative matching family and covering every $P_a$. The maps into $H_n$ have the prescribed factorization and the boundary equations, because $R_a$ is this fibre product. Composition and the fact that open immersions are etale prove the covering assertion.

proof.text: Apply the attachment-operators theorem to the compatible boundary cone of $A_n$; it gives a simplicial extension with strict old restriction and top family equal to $A_n$ plus one copy of each old nondegenerate component for each proper surjection $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$. The splitness theorem applies: the operator theorem gives exactly its epi-label and invertibility hypotheses. The new indices are precisely those of $A_n$. The top matching arrow is a covering: the new family already covers each $P_a$, and adjoining extra arrows preserves joint surjectivity. All its components remain affine and etale over $T$.

source.place: 0DAV (lemma-hypercovering-object), attachment and omitted composition verification, supplied by the cited operator theorem; 0DAU (lemma-split)

proof.text: Extend the map to $H$ by the map $A_n\to H_n$ on new summands and by $H(\sigma)\circ f_r$ on the old summand labelled $(\sigma,i)$, using the inverse normalization isomorphism to the degree-$r$ nondegenerate component. Naturality for faces on new summands is the relative matching equation. On old summands it is naturality of $f$ in retained degrees and $H(\alpha)H(\sigma)=H(\sigma\alpha)$. For degeneracies it is the same identity with concatenated surjections; these are the precise operators of the attachment theorem. Every ordinal map factors as a surjection followed by an injection, so these equations check all naturality squares. This proves the induction with its map to $H$ and its prescribed new-summand factorizations.

source.place: 0DAV (lemma-hypercovering-object), explicit normalized operators; relative refinement verification

proof.text: Choose these extensions recursively. Put $K_q$ equal to the degree-$q$ term of the stage through $q$; define an operator between degrees $q,r$ at the stage through $\max(q,r)$. Strict restriction makes this independent of any later stage. A composition uses only three degrees, so its equality is the functor law at their maximum. The same argument gives $K\to H$. Each matching diagram uses only lower degrees, so its matching covering is the one already verified at that stage. Every index set and coproduct lies in the size bound: finite products of chosen sets and countably many recursion stages are sets in the ambient universe. The resulting $K$ is a full formal-family hypercover, with the asserted epi-index splitting.

Realize every family by its scheme coproduct, giving $V_q=\coprod_iK_{q,i}$. The componentwise maps glue uniquely to a simplicial scheme. To compare matching limits, for family maps $U\to W\leftarrow Z$ the inverse images of the disjoint open pieces $U_i,W_j,Z_k$ partition the scheme fibre product into the pieces $U_i\times_{W_j}Z_k$ with matching indices. These pieces cover: each point selects its two source indices, whose target indices must agree. Their universal mapping properties and gluing identify this partition with the formal-family fibre-product formula. The singleton terminal family realizes to $T$. Iterating terminal objects and fibre products therefore identifies every realized finite matching limit with the scheme matching limit, compatibly with projections and matching arrows. Component arrows are etale by cancellation between etale $T$-schemes, and their coproduct arrow is etale by locality on the source. It is surjective because each target component is covered. Thus every $V_n\to M_n(V/T)$ is surjective etale, and every $V_n\to T$ is etale. The realized map to $H$ retains the prescribed nondegenerate factorizations.

proof.text: For existence without a target take the constant simplicial $T$-scheme $H$: its matching maps are identities, so it is a hypercover. For an arbitrary algebraic space $X\to T$, fibre products exist and the cited space theorem preserves surjective etale families by base change. The universal property gives $M_n(X\times_TV/X)\cong X\times_TM_n(V/T)$: both classify the same finite compatible families of maps from any test space over $X$; this includes $n=0$. Thus each new matching arrow is the base change of a surjective etale arrow. The decomposition also pulls back: on every scheme test object its pieces are the inverse images of the disjoint open summands, and are a disjoint open cover, so the coproduct comparison is an isomorphism by gluing; this identifies the space coproduct by its mapping property. Its components need not remain affine or even schemes, and neither is asserted. None of the argument selects finite subcovers or assumes quasi-separatedness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q77-5453b4c81 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Split with no new nodes; 8 steps, each read against the statements it cites. Statement correction checked: the base clause requiring every component to factor through prescribed affine covers is false. Counterexample: T=A^1_C, H constant, degree-n covers {D(t-a_n),D(t-b_n)} over infinitely many disjoint pairs. The open image of a summand V_{0,i} would have to omit infinitely many closed points, which no nonempty open of A^1 does. The corrected clause asks the factorisation only of nondegenerate summands; that is exactly the freedom of Stacks 0DAV (hypercovering.tex l.2580ff, which covers the new matching pieces). The only citer, lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality (steps 3 and 5), does not use the clause. The correction is named in the report and split_report. Step checks: step 1 FC finite limits/proper-face matching, singleton matching = {M_n(H)}; step 2 affine basis plus covering composition; step 3 R_a=P_a×_{M_n(H)}H_n, via covering base change, with no affine-intersection assumption; step 4 attachment-operators conclusions = attachment-split hypotheses, with adjoined degenerate arrows étale by cancellation; steps 5-6 routine naturality and strict-restriction assembly; step 7 the fibre product of coproducts is the disjoint union of compatible pieces (gluing), étale by local-on-source; step 8 algebraic-space base change and matching commutation. Edge cases tested: T=Spec k, T empty, n=1, non-qc T. Duplicate search: the qcqs finite-split hypercover nodes are strictly more restrictive and the pro-étale existence node is a different setting, so none is a duplicate. No SGA. tool_uses accepted as generic. Batch-5: lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers (Stacks 02X2/041F) is a generic algebraic-space fibre-product fact, not part of the proof of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so accepted.
